title: Install Quiet Hours Handbook - April 2026
body:
Purpose
This is a working handbook for the team running installs during off-peak / quiet hours windows. It collects patterns we see in the field, timings that matter, common noisy failures that only happen at 03:00 local, and a lightweight coordination checklist so on-call and install engineers can run with fewer interruptions. Treat as living notes — copy sections into ticket templates or handoff notes as needed.

Context and motivation
- Several recent installs (multiple customers in EMEA and APAC) have expected low-impact changes during their local night windows. We keep hitting a few recurring issues that waste the quiet window: NTP drift, intermittent DHCP/NIC renumbering, and preflight misreads of the on-prem proxy certs.
- Goal: reduce surprise work in the 00:00–06:00 local window and provide a standard routine that field engineers and the on-call SRE can follow without pulling the whole team.

Quiet-hours install play pattern (recommended cadence)
1) 18–24 hours pre-window: customer preflight email from SE/PM with explicit contact numbers and emergency escalation path (include local site manager).
2) 6 hours pre-window: automated config snapshot from customer (if available) and sanity check against expected CIDR/MTU/NTP settings. Flag mismatches to SE and ask for 2-hour remediation SLA.
3) 60 minutes pre-window: kick off remote health checks from our agent (commands we run: curl /health, docker ps, systemctl status redwood-agent). Paste outputs into the ticket.
4) T-minus 15: set up ephemeral logging session: tcpdump on NIC, journald follow, and start a short iPerf 10s to baseline throughput.
5) Window execution: one-hour blocks with a single owner. If task runs longer than 1 hour, rotate but produce a concise handoff note.

Common friction points (field-observed, April patch cycle)
- NTP drift: customer infra often blocks outbound NTP and we rely on internal stratum that is misconfigured. Symptom: token validation errors on GC nodes after 30m. Quick mitigation: force systemd-timesyncd restart and verify /etc/adjtime; long-term: ask customer to open NTP to our vetted pool or install local NTP server.
- DHCP renumbering during reboots: Some on-prem switches are set to low lease times; reboot during install causes new IP assignment and our node manifests fail to reconcile. Workaround: static DHCP reservation or temporary static assignment for the install window.
- Proxy TLS interception: local corporate proxies resign certs. When we fetch model artifacts at pull time, curl fails with cert mismatch. We add the proxy CA to the container store for the window and then revert. Note: record the CA hash in ticket.
- Disk pressure under /var/lib/containers: older servers were provisioned with small root lvs. When pulling quantized models, we'll run out of space. Prioritize 'du -sh' before pull. If <30GB available, raise a preflight red flag.

Rapid triage checklist (if something goes sideways)
- Step 0: snapshot logs (journalctl -u redwood-agent --no-pager > /tmp/agent.log) and immediately push to the ticket.
- Step 1: check networking (ip a; ip route; ss -tunlp) and confirm IPs expected.
- Step 2: confirm model artifact accessibility (curl -I <artifact url>) and certificate chain.
- Step 3: if KV cache fail or cold start stall, try restart of serving process with preserved /kv cache mount; avoid full wipe during quiet hours.
- Step 4: escalate to on-call SRE if node enters CrashLoopBackOff and restart_count > 5 in 20 minutes. Include diagnostic bundle link.

Example recent incident (concise)
- Customer: Meridian Health (pseudonym)
- Window: Apr 2 03:00–06:00 BST
- Symptom: All inference nodes lost network after a puppet run; K8s node rejoined with different IP and pods failed to mount PVCs.
- Root cause: Puppet applied a vendor firmware patch that changed switch DHCP behavior.
- Fix applied: temporary static assignment + remap in /etc/hosts for the install window + rebind PVCs. Post-mortem: add vendor firmware check to 24-hour preflight.

Hand-off template (fill into ticket when rotating owner)
- Owner: [name]
- Time range: [start]–[end] UTC
- Summary of actions taken: [short bullets]
- Outstanding risks: [e.g. swap pressure, proxy cert missing]
- Next steps / who to wake: [name and phone]

Open questions and known unknowns
- Should we allow installs to proceed when preflight shows <25GB root free? Trade-off: customer business window vs risk of late artifact fetch failures. Proposal: require explicit SE sign-off in ticket if <25GB.
- Do we want to automate the CA import/revert for proxy-intercepted installs? Idea: ephemeral container that mounts host cert store, injects CA, then removes it. Needs safety review.

Action items (April follow-ups)
- Priya: add the 24h vendor firmware check to preflight template (JIRA-PLAT-4821) — due Apr 10.
- Ethan: script for snapshotting journalctl + tcpdump and auto-upload to ticket (prototype by Apr 16).
- Maya: update handoff ticket template with explicit static-IP mitigation steps (review Apr 12).
- Liam: draft brief for SEs outlining when to require static DHCP reservation (in progress).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the checklist short — we consistently ignore >7-step lists in live windows.
- Remind SEs to include local site phone; Slack pings don't cut it when a switch tech needs to be on site.
- Consider a small "install kit" zip with CA import script, disk-check script, and ipfix snapshot helper.

Appendix: quick commands to paste in ticket
- agent status: systemctl status redwood-agent --no-pager
- logs: journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 500 --no-pager > /tmp/agent.log
- disk: df -h /var/lib/containers
- net: ip a; ip route; ss -tunlp
- cert chain: openssl s_client -showcerts -connect <host>:443

End of doc — please add notes or edits inline.
